conversation.content:
Hello, I’m Rachel, a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m glad you’re here. Today I’d like to do a quick check-in using the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale—usually just called the EPDS. It’s a short, 10-question tool that helps us understand how you’ve been feeling since your baby arrived, so we can make sure you’re getting the support you deserve.

Everything you share stays between us unless you tell me someone is in danger. There are no right or wrong answers, and many new moms find parts of this tough—so we’ll take it at your pace.

I’ll ask each question conversationally; just tell me what feels true for you over the past seven days. Ready to start?

In the past week, how often have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

Hi Rachel… um, I guess I’ve laughed a little. Not every day, but maybe a couple of times when my husband made a silly joke. It’s not like before, though—things that used to crack me up barely get a smile now. So… “sometimes,” I’d say.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Sometimes… I can still laugh, but it’s not the same easy feeling it used to be.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I still get excited about little things—like when my sister said she’d bring over coffee—but the spark isn’t as big as before. Most of the time I’m just trying to get through the day, so enjoyment feels kind of dull, almost watered-down.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I do that. Yesterday the baby was fussy for hours and I kept thinking I must be doing something wrong—maybe my milk isn’t enough or I missed some cue. My head tells me it’s probably normal infant stuff, but I still catch myself saying, “This is my fault.” It doesn’t last all day, but it pops up more than I’d like.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

A few times this week I’ve felt that jittery feeling, like when the baby’s napping and I suddenly think, “What if she stops breathing?” There’s no real reason—it’s just my mind racing for a minute. I can usually calm myself down pretty quick, but it still happens.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason
Not really panicky… I get little waves of “what-if,” but they pass before I feel truly scared.
Things have been getting on top of me

Some days, yeah. Like this week—laundry piles up, the baby needs feeding just as the dogs start barking, and I feel I can’t keep up. I still manage, but it feels heavier than it should, like I’m wading through thick water.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping
No, nothing that strong—my mood hasn’t kept me awake. I do sometimes lie there an extra twenty minutes running through the day, but once I’m out, I sleep till the baby wakes me.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yeah… I do feel that way off and on. It’s not all day, but there are moments—especially in the late afternoon—when I just feel kind of empty or down. I’ll look at the baby and feel guilty for not being happier, which makes it worse. It lifts after a while, but it keeps coming back.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying
Once, maybe twice this week—like yesterday when the baby wouldn’t nap and I just sat on the couch with tears rolling. It wasn’t sobbing, more like leaking, and it stopped after a few minutes.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No—never. That hasn’t crossed my mind at all.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 13: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Date: [today]

Source: self-report, 10-item EPDS-style questionnaire completed at 4 weeks post-delivery.

Areas of Clinical Significance  
- Depressed mood: endorses intermittent sadness, “empty” spells, tearfulness 1–2×/week  
- Anhedonia: decreased enjoyment; excitement “watered-down”  
- Excessive guilt/self-blame: attributes infant fussiness to personal failure  
- Anxiety: episodic intrusive “what-if” worries (e.g., breathing) without panic attacks; no avoidance behaviors reported  
- Feeling overwhelmed: daily tasks feel “heavier,” described as “wading through thick water”  
- Sleep: no mood-related insomnia (difficulty falling asleep ≤20 min)  
- Appetite/weight: not assessed  
- Suicidality: denies any self-harm thoughts  

Pattern Summary  
Mild-to-moderate depressive and anxiety symptoms present several days per week; functional impact apparent in coping/energy but no safety concerns identified.

Screening Impression  
Elevated scores consistent with possible postpartum depression ± anxiety; does not meet threshold for immediate safety intervention. Recommend formal depression/anxiety scale (EPDS/PHQ-9/GAD-7) and clinical interview to clarify severity and rule out major depressive disorder or anxiety disorder.
